title: Why Medical AI Needs a Referee | Protege's Engy Ziedan
content: Medical AI faces a measurement problem: high benchmark scores do not guarantee real-world clinical readiness. Engy Ziedan of Protege argues for independent evaluations that assess actual workflow performance rather than static tests. Risks include subtle bias, prompt-dependent ranking variability, and misalignment between benchmarks and clinical needs. Contaminated training data can distort benchmarks. As AI becomes more personalized and evolves rapidly, continuous monitoring may be needed instead of periodic testing.

title: 折叠 iPhone 最全爆料汇总：用过的都说好，但有两个大缺点
content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone will be a book-style device with a 5.5-inch outer screen and 7.8-inch inner screen, featuring a nearly invisible crease and slim 4.5mm profile when unfolded. Early testers praised the pocketable size and hinge durability, while the expanded interface adopts an iPad-like layout powered by iOS 27's new adaptive design framework.

However, two major compromises stand out: no telephoto camera—only main and ultra-wide lenses—and the replacement of Face ID with side-mounted Touch ID to save internal space. Priced above $2,000, this niche debut product prioritizes foldable form factor over Pro-tier features, targeting wealthy early adopters rather than mass consumers, particularly in China, the world's largest foldable market.

title: Anthropic滑跪认错，Claude暗中降智实锤
content: Developer argofowl discovered that Claude Code 2.1.237+ was mapping "high" reasoning effort to "10" (previously "low") due to an unannounced A/B test by Anthropic. Engineer Thariq Shihipar acknowledged the experiment but denied performance impact. Separately, users reported significant degradation in Opus 5's output quality, with Shihipar admitting its instability is a top priority. The incident highlights a broader industry problem: benchmark scores rise while user experience declines, and opaque server-side changes to AI models undermine developer trust lacking version transparency or rollback mechanisms.

content: Oura faces a class-action lawsuit by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco for allegedly exaggerating its smart ring's sleep tracking accuracy.
